case_title: Sayaji Hanmat Sankar v. State of Maharashtra
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 302 IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment
neutral_facts: The accused came home under the influence of liquor and started abusing his wife. There was a petty quarrel between them, and in the course of the quarrel, the accused hit his wife on the left knee with a brass pot and then threw a burning kerosene lamp on her. The victim was wearing a nylon sari, which caught fire and caused her to be engulfed in flames. She was taken to the hospital, where she was found to have sustained burns covering 70% of her body. In her dying declaration, she stated that the accused had tried to douse the fire. The accused also sustained burn injuries covering 18% of his body. The prosecution relied on the dying declaration to establish the accused's intent to cause death or grievous harm, leading to a conviction under Section 302 IPC. However, the Supreme Court found that the act was committed in the heat of passion during a sudden quarrel without premeditation, and therefore, the conviction was modified to Section 304 Part I IPC, with the sentence reduced to the period already served.
